Use legacy FEniCS (dolfin) with small-strain linear elasticity solved as a 2D plane-stress variational problem with a vector-valued displacement space and a direct linear solver.
Model a plain 1 m × 0.5 m rectangular plate of unit thickness with a single circular hole of radius 0.1 m centered at (0.5, 0.25); make no other geometric features.
Mesh the plate with 64 elements per edge.
Use material properties E = 70e9 Pa, ν = 0.33, ρ = 2700 kg/m³, and gravity g = 9.81 m/s² acting as a body force (−ρ g in y).
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law for the 2D stress-strain relation.
Fully clamp the left edge x = 0 by prescribing u = (0, 0) on the entire edge (both components zero).
Apply a torque of M = 800 Nm as a tangential traction on the half-disc region of radius r = 0.02 m centered at (1, 0.25), clipped by the right edge x = 1, with the plate geometry left as a plain rectangle.
Compute the base tangential traction as t_θ = M/(2πr) = 800/(2π·0.02) ≈ 6366 N/m² and multiply it by 2 on the half-disc facets so the resultant applied moment equals exactly 800 Nm.
Apply the traction in the local tangential direction around the center point (1, 0.25), not a fixed global direction.
Keep the hole boundary traction-free, and keep all other boundaries traction-free except the clamped left edge and gravity.
Verify the resultant applied moment after assembly by integrating r × t over the loaded facets and confirming it equals approximately 800 Nm.
Verify the reaction moment at the clamped left edge is approximately −800 Nm plus gravity contributions.
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane Cauchy stress field.
Output and analyze the displacement field and von Mises stress patterns under the combined gravity and rotational loading, including stress concentrations near the hole and the clamp.
